settings.name: Dr Richie Barclay, Founder · PhD, cell biology and nutrition

settings.text: Most of the people I’ve worked with in their 40s and 50s were doing everything right, and still buying on a leap of faith. Labels that didn’t show the doses. Nobody checking every batch.
So when I built MUTO, I built it the way I’d want it built for my own family: nothing hidden, everything checkable.

settings.title: Can I see your test results?
settings.text: Yes. Batch certificates are available on request: hello@mutolongevity.com.

settings.title: Why NR and not NMN?
settings.text: NR is authorised for food supplements in Great Britain, at up to 300mg a day for adults. NMN is still under novel food assessment.

settings.title: Has MUTO been clinically proven?
settings.text: No, and we won’t say it has. Our first human study starts in December 2026 at the University of Westminster. We’ll publish the results, whatever they show.

settings.title: Is it tested for banned substances?
settings.text: Every batch is third-party tested. We don’t currently make a banned-substance certification claim, and we’ll update this page if that changes.

settings.title: Is it safe with medication?
settings.text: Check with your GP or pharmacist first. MUTO contains vitamin K2, which can affect blood thinners such as warfarin.
